name: magicdns-hostname
description:
Tailscale exposes two names and they are not interchangeable. `name` is the MagicDNS FQDN, always a valid DNS label chain. `hostname` is the raw machine name the OS reports, which on a Mac or Windows laptop routinely contains spaces, apostrophes, and parentheses -- "Fixture's Work Laptop (2)" is the default macOS naming pattern. Feeding that into hostnames produces a value runZero rejects as bogus, so the device lands with no usable name at all.

This locks the split: hostnames comes from the MagicDNS name, and the raw machine name is preserved as tailscale_machine_name so nothing is lost. Also covers the DERP latency shape -- each region maps to an object {"latencyMs": float, "preferred": bool}, not a bare number, so stringifying the whole object put a Starlark dict repr into an attribute instead of a searchable number.

Skips namespaced_ids for the reason recorded in happy: no API-provided tailnet scope exists, and the Tailscale-minted device id is already unique across tailnets.
